The formerly unrun source B04 finite derived-key lane has since been replayed: the planted control ranks first among 1,385,600 settings, and none of 6,224,000 bounded LP2 short-text decodes reaches its fixed score bar. This does not test every short seed, key generator or possible decoding rule.

An independent finite-key example and the exact uniform-additive-key comparison distinguish expected adjacent-repeat bounds from impossibility claims about every finite ciphertext or every plaintext-independent key.

unresolved_parts: The exact D3 command is a synthetic, known-seed, key-skip plant. It neither identifies the LP2 cipher nor shows LP2 has a recoverable seed.

B4/G5 reports no separation in a selected six-statistic, 40-realization-per-model simulation (maximum absolute z 1.603). Its original KJV corpus is absent from pinned Git, so this G5 result is source-reported rather than freshly replayed. Finite non-separation is not an information-theoretic or universal ciphertext-indistinguishability proof.
B4/G5 uses output-aware value resampling, while D3 uses key-position skips. The source treats them as one filter family, but the two operations differ.

B4 model A is generated by Python random.Random seeds, not evidence that a true independent one-time pad produced LP2. The original source G4 also places measured LP2 outside model A on diagonal coefficient of variation; a categorical external-pad or derived-key identification is unwarranted.
The later B04 and KDF replays cover named finite dictionaries and decoder settings only; other seeds, generators, plaintext representations and keys remain outside their scope.

unresolved_parts: The source ledger marks this absolute verdict superseded by VERDICT-OTP-CLASS. The D3 plant shows only that one constructed short-seed ciphertext can be recovered when its seed is supplied and a matching decoder is used.

Neither the D3 plant nor B4/G5 finite feature non-separation proves actual LP2 recoverability, or that LP2 uses a truly random independent unreused pad. The information-theoretic conditions for a one-time-pad impossibility claim are not established for LP2.
The now-executed B04 finite search has no score-bar hit within its settings, but that result cannot promote a wider method class to impossible or validate this superseded absolute verdict.
